title: Paranormal activity investigated in Erie County
content:
By Michael Stafford

Correspondent

As the spookiest time of the year approaches, a local paranormal investigator is sharing his ghost encounter experiences. 

“How many people believe in ghosts?” asked James McCann as he began a recent presentation in the darkness of the Little Church on the Hill in Cranesville.

A number of hands went up.

“How many are on the fence?” he continued.

Other hands went up in the air.

Most attendees in the church had an interest in seeing something that could reinforce their beliefs in the paranormal.

McCann, who is a paranormal investigator, recently held a screening of his second film titled “There’s Still Nobody at the Bridge.” The film showed parts of the investigations and evidence McCann and others have gathered in years of investigating paranormal activity at Gudgeonville Bridge, which crosses Elk Creek in Girard Township.

The screening and the presentation that McCann gave were one of the 2026 speaker series that the society holds at the church. Each month throughout the year, a different speaker on a variety of topics gives a presentation for anyone interested in coming.

For October, McCann was the speaker. After showing his film to the audience of more than 40, he showed other evidence including photos and recordings that he has gathered over the years. Many in the audience spoke about their own experiences with the supernatural and asked McCann different questions.

After the presentation, McCann explained his background and what got him interested in investigating the paranormal.

McCann’s interest in the paranormal goes back many years and he recalled that, early in life, the subject had fascinated him. He said that, as a child, he enjoyed the Halloween season and always had an interest in ghosts. For a time in his life he lived in New Orleans, Louisiana, and would go on ghost tours offered in that city. After a chilling experience on one of the tours, McCann’s interest deepened and he began reading books and articles on the internet concerning ghosts and spirits.

When McCann moved back to Erie, he joined a paranormal investigation group, although that group was only short lived.

“I decided I wanted more of this, so I formed my own group,” he said.

The group, called A Paranormal Group Erie County Pa (abbreviated as A.P.G.E.C.P.) took shape in 2003, and he explained that it is a loosely knit together group that investigates different locations for evidence of paranormal activity. The members partake in the investigations when they can fit them into their schedule.

“It’s people that want to get together and go out on an investigation,” he said.

Those investigations aren’t quite like ones that people may see on the internet or on television. McCann explained that much of the time spent on an investigation is sitting around and waiting for something to happen. It’s an activity that requires a good deal of patience.

McCann’s interest in Gudgeonville goes back to his teenage years when he would visit the location as he was intrigued with it.

“Little did I know that 40 years later I would be a paranormal investigator investigating it,” he said. “I’ve had my experiences out there and I thought to myself how could I put this more out there?”

That was when the idea for a film came about. He explained that, not only did he want to share his experiences, but he wanted to prove to people that the area around Gudgeonville is, indeed, haunted. Through meeting a director at the Erie Horrorfest and conversations, the two decided to create the film, which was called, “There’s Nobody at the Bridge.” In it, McCann shares his experiences near the bridge and others share stories as well.

“At the end of it, we kind of leave people hanging, wanting more,” he said.

Inasmuch, McCann decided that a sequel should be created. In the second film titled “There’s Still Nobody at the Bridge” he said that more evidence was put into the content to help people understand that there is something paranormal about the area. He said he wanted it to be a documentary.

“I wanted to put it across that it’s real,” he said. “It’s not jump scares you see on YouTube or TV. I tried to be direct.”

In the film, which was the one shown at the Little Church on the Hill, photos and recordings are shown and played and others speak about how spirits can make such transmissions and how they are detected. Additionally, the film also cites two deaths that actually occurred at the site of the bridge, including the tragic fall of 10-year-old Darlene Nichols of Girard from the cliffs above Elk Creek in April 1964. The other death that occurred in a similar way was that of 15-year-old Ruby Shorts from Union City in September 1955, when she also fell from the cliffs above Elk Creek.

The film also notes the prediction that McCann once received a year before the old Gudgeonville Covered Bridge was destroyed by arsonists, as well as an experience he had with seeing lights on the opposite side of the bridge, which he said could not be explained.

McCann also gave credit to Tom Balos, who edited the second film.

“All in all, I think it came out good. We worked hard on it,” he said.

The screening of the film at the church this month was not the first time McCann has been there. He explained that, at one point, he investigated the church building for evidence of paranormal activity. In doing so, he made friends with a caretaker of the church who suggested he be the speaker at one of the monthly events held by the Elk Creek Historical Society. Since then, he has been coming out each year, around October.

As for whether there is another movie in the works, McCann said that he does not know if there would be any more. What will continue, though, is McCann’s investigations of the Gudgeonville Bridge. As McCann has investigated nearly every potential haunted location in Erie County, he said he enjoys going to farther locations, including those out of state.

“I like going every where,” he said.

Editor’s note: For those interested in learning more about the paranormal group or contacting McCann, he has both a presence on Facebook and a Youtube channel.
